title.en: The accusative case: objects and directions

card: The accusative marks the **direct object** (*I read **a book***), and after **в/на** it means *into/onto* (куда́?). Only feminine **-а/-я** nouns visibly change in the singular: **кни́га → кни́гу**, **неде́ля → неде́лю**. Masculine **animate** nouns look like the genitive: **ви́жу бра́та**.

sections.body: The accusative is the case of the thing directly affected by the action. The good news is how little it changes: masculine inanimate and neuter nouns, and feminine **-ь** nouns, look exactly like the nominative. Only two groups need attention: feminine nouns in **-а/-я**, and animate masculine nouns (people and animals).

sections.title: Animacy: why ви́жу бра́та
sections.body:
Russian distinguishes living beings from things in the accusative. For masculine nouns in the singular, and for **all** nouns in the plural, an animate accusative borrows the genitive form: **Я ви́жу бра́та.** **Я ви́жу студе́нтов.** **Я люблю́ ко́шек.** An inanimate accusative copies the nominative: **Я ви́жу стол.** **Я ви́жу столы́.**

The rule exists because, in old Russian, **Оте́ц лю́бит сын** could not show who loved whom (the two forms were identical), so the genitive form was borrowed to make the object clear.

sections.title: Direction and time
sections.body:
After **в** and **на**, the accusative answers **куда́?** (*where to?*): **Я иду́ в шко́лу.** **Положи́ кни́гу на стол.** Compare the prepositional for location: **Я в шко́ле.** **Кни́га на столе́.**

The accusative also gives points and stretches of time: **в сре́ду** (*on Wednesday*), **всю неде́лю** (*all week*), **ка́ждый день** (*every day*).

English has an accusative only in pronouns: *she → her*, *they → them*. If *him* or *her* would fit in English, think accusative in Russian. The Russian pronouns: **меня́, тебя́, его́, её, нас, вас, их**.

**куда́? → accusative; где? → prepositional.** A ball thrown **into** the box flies (accusative); a ball lying **in** the box sits still (prepositional). The accusative ending **-у** is like an arrow pointing at the target.

mistakes.why: **брат** is animate, so the accusative looks like the genitive.
Going *to* a place is direction (куда́?), so accusative.
The book is the direct object.

examples.en: Put the key on the table.
